PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Your school has its own story, its own values, a motto and rules. In this sub-strand you will find out and narrate the history of your school, explain its values, recite its motto and learn why obeying school rules keeps the school orderly and safe.

## Strand 3.0: Social Organisations
Sub-strand 3.2: The School
Suggested lessons: 3

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Social Studies Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 Social Organisations, Sub-strand 3.2 The School
• KICD Grade 4 Social Studies radio lesson: The School

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) narrate the history of the school
b) explain the values of the school
c) recite the school motto
d) desire to obey the school rules

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why is it important to maintain discipline in school?

PAGE 2: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• gather information on the history of the school from relevant personnel and share in class
• discuss the history of the school with others in class
• use digital or print resources to find out the school values
• develop a poster on the school values
• develop a poster on the school motto and display it in class
• make a gallery walk and peer assess

## Core competencies
• Communication and collaboration: Learners recite the school motto
• Citizenship: Learners gather information on the history of the school from the school administration and share in class

## Values
• Integrity: Learners exhibit discipline as they display, make a gallery walk and peer assess.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social cohesion: Learners develop charts to explain the school values

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative arts: Learners apply graphic designing in Creative Arts in the designing of school motto and rules

PAGE 3: Lesson 1: The history of our school

LESSON 1: THE HISTORY OF OUR SCHOOL
===================================

## What you will learn
• Gather information on the history of the school from relevant people.
• Narrate the history of the school in the correct order of events.

Curriculum outcomes: a) narrate the history of the school

## Introduction
Every school was started by someone, at some time, for a reason. The classrooms you learn in today may have begun as one small room or even a class under a tree.

## Notes

A school is a place where learners are taught under the guidance of teachers. The history of a school is the story of how it started and how it has grown over the years.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: The history of our school — What to find out

### What to find out
When you study the history of your school, try to answer these questions:

- When was the school started?
- Who started it? It may have been started by the community, a religious organisation, the government or a group of parents.
- Why was it started? For example, children may have been walking long distances to the nearest school.
- Who was the first head teacher, and how many learners and teachers were there at the beginning?
- How has the school changed? Think about new classrooms, a library, a playground, water tanks, electricity or computers.
- What important events have happened, such as the first national examination, sports achievements or visits by important guests?

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: The history of our school — Where to get the information

### Where to get the information
You can gather information from relevant personnel, which means people who know the facts. These include:

- The head teacher and deputy head teacher
- Teachers who have worked in the school for a long time
- Members of the school board of management and parents
- Former learners of the school
- Elders in the community who saw the school start
- School records such as the log book, admission register and photographs

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: The history of our school — Narrating the history

### Narrating the history
To narrate is to tell a story in order. Start with how the school began, then tell the important changes in the order they happened, and end with what the school is like today. A timeline helps you keep events in the right order.

## Key words
• history — the story of past events
• narrate — to tell a story in the order in which things happened
• timeline — a line that shows events in the order they happened

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Name two people who can tell you about the history of your school.

Working:
1. Think of people who have been at the school for a long time or who keep records.

Answer: Any two, for example the head teacher, a long-serving teacher, a former learner or an elder in the community.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: The history of our school — Interview on the school's history

## Activity: Interview on the school's history
You will need: Exercise book, Pen, Manila paper for a timeline

1. As a class, prepare questions about when, how and why the school was started.

2. In groups, interview the head teacher, a long-serving teacher or another relevant person. Be polite and thank them.

3. Write down the answers and share them in class.

4. Draw a timeline showing the main events in the history of the school.

5. Take turns to narrate the history of the school to your group.

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: The history of our school — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. What is the history of a school?

2. Name one school record that can help you learn about the school's history.

3. What does it mean to narrate?

## Answers to practice

1. The story of how the school started and how it has grown over the years.

2. The log book, admission register or old photographs.

3. To tell a story in the order in which things happened.

## Summary
• The history of a school tells when, how and why it started and how it has grown.
• Relevant personnel and school records give correct information.
• Narrate the events in the order they happened.

PAGE 9: Lesson 2: School values and the school motto

LESSON 2: SCHOOL VALUES AND THE SCHOOL MOTTO
============================================

## What you will learn
• Explain the values of the school.
• Recite the school motto and explain its meaning.

Curriculum outcomes: b) explain the values of the school; c) recite the school motto

## Introduction
Many schools paint their motto on the gate or the wall of the administration block. It is a short sentence that tells everyone what the school stands for.

## Notes

### School values
Values are beliefs that guide us to do what is right. Each school chooses values that it wants every learner, teacher and worker to live by. Common school values include:

PAGE 10: Lesson 2: School values and the school motto — Notes 2

- Respect: being polite to teachers, workers, visitors and fellow learners, and taking care of other people's property.
- Responsibility: doing your duties, such as cleaning the classroom and finishing homework, without being reminded.
- Honesty: telling the truth and not taking what is not yours.
- Integrity: doing the right thing even when nobody is watching.
- Unity: working together as one school.
- Excellence: always trying to do your best.
- Care and compassion: helping those who are in need, such as a sick or new learner.
- Tolerance: accepting people who are different from you.

You can find out your school's values from the school notice board, the school prospectus, the school website or from your teachers.

PAGE 11: Lesson 2: School values and the school motto — The school motto

### The school motto
A motto is a short sentence or phrase that shows the aim of the school. It reminds learners what they should work towards. Examples of school mottos are:

- Strive for excellence
- Study for service
- Diligence rewards
- Education is light

A motto usually has a meaning that is bigger than its few words. For example, 'Strive for excellence' means always working hard to do your best in everything, from class work to sports.

Knowing your school motto by heart and living by it shows that you are proud of your school. Some schools recite the motto during assembly.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: School values and the school motto — Example 1

## Key words
• value — a belief that guides us to do what is right
• motto — a short sentence that shows the aim of a school or group
• excellence — being very good at something by doing your best

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A learner finds a pen on the floor and hands it to the teacher. Which value is the learner showing?

Working:
1. The learner did not keep what was not theirs.

Answer: Honesty (or integrity).

## Worked examples

### Example 2
Explain the motto 'Study for service'.

Working:
1. Study means learning.
2. Service means helping others.

Answer: Learners should study hard so that they can use their knowledge to serve others.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: School values and the school motto — Values and motto posters

## Activity: Values and motto posters
You will need: Manila paper, Crayons or marker pens, Print or digital resources such as the school prospectus or notice board

1. Use digital or print resources, or ask a teacher, to find out the values of your school.

2. In groups, develop a poster showing the school values with a picture for each value.

3. Develop a second poster with the school motto written in large letters and display it in class.

4. Make a gallery walk to look at other groups' posters and peer assess them: is the motto correct? Are the values explained clearly?

5. Recite the school motto together as a class.

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: School values and the school motto — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. What is a school motto?

2. Name three values that a school may have.

3. Write your school motto and say what it means.

## Answers to practice

1. A short sentence that shows the aim of the school.

2. Any three, for example respect, responsibility, honesty, integrity, unity, excellence, care and tolerance.

3. Learners write their own school motto and explain it in their own words.

## Summary
• Values guide us to do what is right.
• The motto is a short sentence that shows the aim of the school.
• Know your school motto by heart and live by it.

PAGE 15: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules

LESSON 3: OBEYING SCHOOL RULES
==============================

## What you will learn
• State examples of school rules.
• Explain why it is important to maintain discipline in school.

Curriculum outcomes: d) desire to obey the school rules

## Introduction
Imagine a school where everyone arrives at any time, shouts in class and throws litter anywhere. Learning would be very hard. School rules help to prevent this.

## Notes

School rules are guidelines that tell learners how to behave in school. They are made by the school to keep order and to help everyone learn well and stay safe.

PAGE 16: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Examples of school rules

### Examples of school rules
- Arrive at school on time.
- Wear the correct school uniform and keep it clean.
- Respect teachers, workers, visitors and fellow learners.
- Do not fight or bully others.
- Keep the classrooms and compound clean; put litter in the bin.
- Take care of school property such as desks, books and taps.
- Do not leave the school compound without permission.
- Speak politely and do not use bad language.

### Discipline
Discipline means behaving well and following rules even without being watched. A disciplined learner obeys the rules because they understand why the rules are there.

PAGE 17: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Why it is important to maintain discipline in school

### Why it is important to maintain discipline in school
- Learners learn well because there is order and less noise.
- Learners are safe because dangerous behaviour such as fighting is avoided.
- School property lasts longer when it is cared for.
- Learners and teachers live in peace and respect one another.
- Learners build good habits, such as keeping time, that will help them all their life.
- The school gets a good name in the community.

### What happens when rules are broken
When rules are broken, learning is disturbed, property may be damaged and people may get hurt. A learner who breaks a rule may be corrected by a teacher. The aim of correction is to help the learner change, not to harm them.

PAGE 18: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Example 1

## Key words
• school rules — guidelines that tell learners how to behave in school
• discipline — behaving well and following rules even when not watched
• obey — to do what a rule or a person in authority says

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Why should learners arrive at school on time?

Working:
1. Think about what happens when someone is late.

Answer: So that they do not miss lessons or disturb others, and so that they build the habit of keeping time.

PAGE 19: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Our school rules chart

## Activity: Our school rules chart
You will need: Copy of the school rules, Manila paper, Marker pens

1. Read the school rules with your teacher.

2. In groups, choose five rules and write why each one is important.

3. Make a chart and display it in class.

4. Role-play a short scene showing what happens when a rule is obeyed and when it is broken.

5. Discuss as a class: why is it important to maintain discipline in school?

PAGE 20: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Give three examples of school rules.

2. What is discipline?

3. Give two reasons why learners should obey school rules.

## Answers to practice

1. Any three, for example arrive on time, wear the correct uniform, do not fight, keep the school clean, take care of school property.

2. Behaving well and following rules even when nobody is watching.

3. Any two, for example to learn well, to keep safe, to live in peace, to protect school property, to build good habits.

## Summary
• School rules keep order and safety in school.
• Discipline means following rules even when nobody is watching.
• Obeying rules helps learners learn well and live in peace.

PAGE 21: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Who is the best person to ask about when your school was started?
   A. A shopkeeper in town
   B. The head teacher or a long-serving teacher
   C. A new learner
   D. A visitor

2. Which school record can show the history of the school?
   A. The log book
   B. A storybook
   C. A calendar for next year
   D. A football

3. When narrating the history of your school, where should you start?

4. Values are:
   A. Beliefs that guide us to do what is right
   B. Prices of goods
   C. Games played at break
   D. Names of teachers

5. A learner cleans the classroom without being told. Which value is shown?
   A. Responsibility
   B. Greed
   C. Laziness
   D. Pride

6. Which value means accepting people who are different from you?
   A. Excellence
   B. Tolerance
   C. Honesty
   D. Punctuality

7. What is a school motto?
   A. A school bus
   B. A short sentence that shows the aim of the school
   C. A list of learners
   D. A school fee receipt

8. What does the motto 'Strive for excellence' mean?

9. Which of these is a school rule?
   A. Fight when angry
   B. Keep the compound clean
   C. Leave school without permission
   D. Write on desks

10. Give two reasons why it is important to maintain discipline in school.

PAGE 22: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. B. The head teacher or a long-serving teacher
   The head teacher and long-serving teachers know the school's history and can check records.

2. A. The log book
   The log book records important events in the school.

3. With how and when the school began.
   Narrating means telling events in the order they happened.

4. A. Beliefs that guide us to do what is right
   School values guide how learners and teachers behave.

5. A. Responsibility
   Doing your duties without being reminded shows responsibility.

6. B. Tolerance
   Tolerance is accepting and respecting differences.

7. B. A short sentence that shows the aim of the school
   A motto is a short statement of what the school aims for.

8. Always work hard to do your best in everything.
   To strive is to try hard; excellence is being very good.

9. B. Keep the compound clean
   Keeping the compound clean is a common school rule.

10. Any two, for example learners learn well, learners are safe, property lasts longer, there is peace, good habits are built.
   Discipline creates order, safety and peace.

LESSON 3: OBEYING SCHOOL RULES
==============================

## What you will learn
• State examples of school rules.
• Explain why it is important to maintain discipline in school.

Curriculum outcomes: d) desire to obey the school rules

## Introduction
Imagine a school where everyone arrives at any time, shouts in class and throws litter anywhere. Learning would be very hard. School rules help to prevent this.

## Notes

School rules are guidelines that tell learners how to behave in school. They are made by the school to keep order and to help everyone learn well and stay safe.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Examples of school rules
studyPages.body:
### Examples of school rules
- Arrive at school on time.
- Wear the correct school uniform and keep it clean.
- Respect teachers, workers, visitors and fellow learners.
- Do not fight or bully others.
- Keep the classrooms and compound clean; put litter in the bin.
- Take care of school property such as desks, books and taps.
- Do not leave the school compound without permission.
- Speak politely and do not use bad language.

### Discipline
Discipline means behaving well and following rules even without being watched. A disciplined learner obeys the rules because they understand why the rules are there.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Why it is important to maintain discipline in school
studyPages.body:
### Why it is important to maintain discipline in school
- Learners learn well because there is order and less noise.
- Learners are safe because dangerous behaviour such as fighting is avoided.
- School property lasts longer when it is cared for.
- Learners and teachers live in peace and respect one another.
- Learners build good habits, such as keeping time, that will help them all their life.
- The school gets a good name in the community.

### What happens when rules are broken
When rules are broken, learning is disturbed, property may be damaged and people may get hurt. A learner who breaks a rule may be corrected by a teacher. The aim of correction is to help the learner change, not to harm them.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Example 1
studyPages.body:
## Key words
• school rules — guidelines that tell learners how to behave in school
• discipline — behaving well and following rules even when not watched
• obey — to do what a rule or a person in authority says

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Why should learners arrive at school on time?

Working:
1. Think about what happens when someone is late.

Answer: So that they do not miss lessons or disturb others, and so that they build the habit of keeping time.

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Our school rules chart
studyPages.body:
## Activity: Our school rules chart
You will need: Copy of the school rules, Manila paper, Marker pens

1. Read the school rules with your teacher.

2. In groups, choose five rules and write why each one is important.

3. Make a chart and display it in class.

4. Role-play a short scene showing what happens when a rule is obeyed and when it is broken.

5. Discuss as a class: why is it important to maintain discipline in school?

studyPages.title: Lesson 3: Obeying school rules — Answers to practice
studyPages.body:
## Practice

1. Give three examples of school rules.

2. What is discipline?

3. Give two reasons why learners should obey school rules.

## Answers to practice

1. Any three, for example arrive on time, wear the correct uniform, do not fight, keep the school clean, take care of school property.

2. Behaving well and following rules even when nobody is watching.

3. Any two, for example to learn well, to keep safe, to live in peace, to protect school property, to build good habits.

## Summary
• School rules keep order and safety in school.
• Discipline means following rules even when nobody is watching.
• Obeying rules helps learners learn well and live in peace.

studyPages.title: Revision quiz
studyPages.body:
REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Who is the best person to ask about when your school was started?
   A. A shopkeeper in town
   B. The head teacher or a long-serving teacher
   C. A new learner
   D. A visitor

2. Which school record can show the history of the school?
   A. The log book
   B. A storybook
   C. A calendar for next year
   D. A football

3. When narrating the history of your school, where should you start?

4. Values are:
   A. Beliefs that guide us to do what is right
   B. Prices of goods
   C. Games played at break
   D. Names of teachers

5. A learner cleans the classroom without being told. Which value is shown?
   A. Responsibility
   B. Greed
   C. Laziness
   D. Pride

6. Which value means accepting people who are different from you?
   A. Excellence
   B. Tolerance
   C. Honesty
   D. Punctuality

7. What is a school motto?
   A. A school bus
   B. A short sentence that shows the aim of the school
   C. A list of learners
   D. A school fee receipt

8. What does the motto 'Strive for excellence' mean?

9. Which of these is a school rule?
   A. Fight when angry
   B. Keep the compound clean
   C. Leave school without permission
   D. Write on desks

10. Give two reasons why it is important to maintain discipline in school.

studyPages.title: Quiz answers
studyPages.body:
ANSWERS
=======

1. B. The head teacher or a long-serving teacher
   The head teacher and long-serving teachers know the school's history and can check records.

2. A. The log book
   The log book records important events in the school.

3. With how and when the school began.
   Narrating means telling events in the order they happened.

4. A. Beliefs that guide us to do what is right
   School values guide how learners and teachers behave.

5. A. Responsibility
   Doing your duties without being reminded shows responsibility.

6. B. Tolerance
   Tolerance is accepting and respecting differences.

7. B. A short sentence that shows the aim of the school
   A motto is a short statement of what the school aims for.

8. Always work hard to do your best in everything.
   To strive is to try hard; excellence is being very good.

9. B. Keep the compound clean
   Keeping the compound clean is a common school rule.

10. Any two, for example learners learn well, learners are safe, property lasts longer, there is peace, good habits are built.
   Discipline creates order, safety and peace.
